items.title: Rational mixed Hodge structures
items.statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure is a finite-dimensional rational vector space $H$ together with a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the weight filtration, and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of $H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the Hodge filtration, such that for every integer $n$ the filtrations induced by $F$ and by its complex conjugate $\bar F$ on the graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ are $n$-opposed: writing $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ for the image of $F^p\cap W_n$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ and $H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$, one has $$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n,\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n.$$ A morphism of rational mixed Hodge structures is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f\colon H\to K$ with $f(W_nH)\subseteq W_nK$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $n,p$. A pure structure of weight $n$ is the special case $W_{n-1}H=0$, $W_nH=H$. A substructure or quotient carries the induced or quotient filtrations; that the kernel, image and cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is proved in the strictness lemma below and is not part of the definition. The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$. The tensor conventions are $W_n(H\otimes K)=\sum_{a+b=n}W_aH\otimes W_bK$ and $F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{a+b=p}F^aH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^bK_{\mathbb C}$, and the dual conventions are $W_n(H^*)=\{u:u(W_{-n-1}H)=0\}$ and $F^p(H^*_{\mathbb C})=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}$. A pure rational Hodge structure is polarizable if it carries a rational bilinear form of the parity of its weight that pairs only complementary Hodge types and whose Weil-operator Hermitian form is positive definite. No mixed structure is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. Well-definedness: the $n$-opposition is a condition imposed on the given data, and the displayed decomposition defines the summands $H^{p,q}_n$ rather than asserting an identity beyond that axiom; both filtrations are finite and $H$ is finite dimensional, so all sums over $p,q$ in the statement are finite. The clauses on substructures and quotients, on the tensor and dual formulas, and the Tate and polarizability conventions record the structures the later pages use; the definition asserts no existence theorem for them and this batch's proofs use none of them. The forward mention of kernel and image is explanatory only and creates no dependency: the existence statement is the strictness lemma. Choice-free: finite-dimensional linear algebra over $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb C$, no index set is chosen.
items.axiom_use: None: the definition quantifies only over finite filtrations of a finite-dimensional space.

items.title: The Deligne splitting of a mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: Let $(H,W,F)$ be a rational mixed Hodge structure with complex conjugation $\sigma$ on $H_{\mathbb C}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, and write $\bar F^a=\sigma(F^a)$ for the conjugate Hodge filtration. For integers $p,q$ put $m=p+q$ and $$I^{p,q}=\bigl(F^p\cap W_m\bigr)\cap\Bigl((\bar F^q\cap W_m)+\sum_{j\ge1}(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1})\Bigr),$$ the intersections taken in $H_{\mathbb C}$. Then: (a) $I^{p,q}\subseteq W_m\cap F^p$, the intersection $I^{p,q}\cap W_{m-1}$ is zero, and the projection $W_m\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH_{\mathbb C}$ maps $I^{p,q}$ isomorphically onto the summand $H^{p,q}_m$ of the mixed Hodge definition; (b) $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$, $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}$ and $\bar F^bH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}I^{p,q}$ for all integers $a,b,m$, so in particular $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}$; (c) every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. The construction is not conjugate-symmetric in general: the formula need not satisfy $\sigma(I^{p,q})=I^{q,p}$, and no such identity is claimed or used (the sources record only the standard congruence modulo $W_{m-2}$). The splitting is the one pinned down in the sources by the displayed formula, not an arbitrary direct-sum decomposition.
items.strategy: Route (Deligne II 1.2.5, 1.2.8-1.2.11; Voisin Theorem 2.8 and its proof; El Zein Lemma 2.1; Weber (2.2.4)-(2.2.5); cross-check Cirici-Horel Lemma 3.3). Step 1: Deligne's two-filtration lemma. If two finite decreasing filtrations $F,\bar F$ on a finite-dimensional space are $m$-opposed, i.e. $\operatorname{Gr}^p_F\operatorname{Gr}^q_{\bar F}=0$ for $p+q>m$, then the subspaces $A^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$ with $p+q=m$ bigrade the space and $F^p=\bigoplus_{p'\ge p}A^{p',m-p'}$; prove this by descending induction on $p$ from the splitting $F^p=(F^{p+1})+(F^p\cap\bar F^{m-p+1})$, which holds because $p+(m-p+1)=m+1$. Applied on each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ this gives the pieces $H^{p,q}_m$ of the definition and the corresponding decompositions of $F$ and $\bar F$ there. Step 2: the lifting lemma. With $m=p+q$, show that the displayed $I^{p,q}$ is mapped isomorphically onto $H^{p,q}_m$ by $W_m\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$; this is Deligne II 1.2.8, proved by downward induction on the weight together with the elementary algebraic sub-lemma 1.2.9. At each step one takes a representative in $F^p\cap W_{m}$ lifting the wanted graded class, identifies the obstruction to lying in the second factor with an element of the complementary summand supplied by the opposition at the next lower weight, and corrects it; because the weight filtration is finite the corrections terminate. Step 3: sum over the pieces. Since each $I^{p,q}$ projects isomorphically to a distinct summand, the sum map $\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}\to W_m$ is an isomorphism on every associated graded piece, hence an isomorphism by descending induction on $m$; the $F$- and $\bar F$-decompositions follow from the same projection computation in the two-filtration lemma. Step 4: functoriality. A morphism preserves $W$, $F$ and conjugation (hence also $\bar F$), so applying it to the intersection-and-sum formula for $H$ gives an element of the corresponding formula for $K$; no canonicality or uniqueness argument is needed for this. After the proof record the caveat that the formula is not conjugate-symmetric: the sources give only the congruence modulo $W_{m-2}$ (Weber (2.2.5)), and neither exactness nor the congruence is used in this batch. The authored proof must reproduce the induction of Deligne II 1.2.8 in full; only the cited route, not the source text, is offered here.
items.axiom_use: None: the argument is finite-dimensional linear algebra with finite filtrations; no basis or complement is chosen from an infinite family.

items.title: Strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms
items.statement: Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for $W$ and for $F$: $$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$ for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is $W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has pure image of weight $n$.
items.strategy: Apply the Deligne splitting lemma to $H$ and to $K$. Step 1: weight strictness. Let $y=f(x)\in f(H)\cap W_mK$ and decompose $x=\sum_{p,q}x^{p,q}$ and $y=\sum_{p,q}f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ along the splittings; functoriality of the splitting puts $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ in $I^{p,q}(K)$, so the displayed decompositions are the ones supplied by the lemma. As $y\in W_mK$ means $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ whenever $p+q>m$, one has $y=f(\sum_{p+q\le m}x^{p,q})$ with $\sum_{p+q\le m}x^{p,q}\in W_mH$. Step 2: Hodge strictness is the same computation with the condition $p<a$ instead of $p+q>m$: an element of $f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^aK_{\mathbb C}$ is the image of the sum of the $I^{p,q}$-components with $p\ge a$, which lies in $F^aH_{\mathbb C}$. Step 3: the rational equality follows from the complex one because both sides are complexifications of rational subspaces and the comparison maps are isomorphisms. Step 4: kernel, image and cokernel. The kernel and image are compatible with the bigraded decompositions: on each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ the induced or quotient filtration is the restriction or quotient of the $(p,q)$-bigrading $H^{p,q}_m$, and a subspace or quotient of an $m$-opposed pair that is compatible with the bigrading is again $m$-opposed, with the conjugate of the $(p,q)$-piece equal to the $(q,p)$-piece; this is the argument of Deligne II 1.2.12 and 2.3.5(ii). Hence the induced and quotient filtrations satisfy the mixed Hodge axioms, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact because it is exact on each weight level by weight strictness. Step 5: the pure-image statement: if $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nK=K$, then $W_{n-1}\operatorname{im}f=f(W_{n-1}H)=0$ and $W_n\operatorname{im}f=\operatorname{im}f\cap W_nK=\operatorname{im}f$, so the image is pure of weight $n$. The statement deliberately claims no splitting or uniqueness of the induced structures.
items.axiom_use: None: finite-dimensional linear algebra and the preceding splitting lemma.

items.title: Cohomological mixed Hodge complexes
items.statement: A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex consists of: (a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each cochain group; (b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ by subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group; (c) a filtered comparison morphism $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$ which is a quasi-isomorphism; subject to the axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its induced differential is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational comparison, is a pure Hodge structure of weight $r+w$. The weight filtration on $H^n(K)$ is the shifted filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr)$; this shift is essential and pole-count weight on a logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The same definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a space when the complexes are replaced by derived global sections and the required resolutions preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are constructed, not here.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The axiom is a condition on the data (Deligne III (8.1.5) together with (8.1.1)-(8.1.2)); the displayed shift is the convention of (1.1.2), and it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ compatible with the weight of $H^n$; the statement records this rather than proving it. The strictness requirement on the differentials of the graded complexes is exactly axiom (GH1); the standard equivalent formulation, that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at its first page, is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used here, so no degeneration theorem enters the dependencies. Biregularity (finiteness on each cochain group) is what the filtered-complex comparison needs in the following lemma; it holds for the complexes occurring in this run. The sheaf clause is applied by resolving the graded pieces separately; a Godement resolution of a complex of sheaves has exact terms and successive cokernels, so it preserves the graded pieces, but the proof of that statement belongs to the pages that construct the sheaves. Choice-free at this level: no family of nonempty sets is selected.
items.axiom_use: None in the definition itself; the later pages that build sheaf resolutions must declare their own choice use.

items.title: Mixed Hodge complex cohomology and cosimplicial weights
items.statement: (i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex. Then for every $n$ the vector space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight filtration is the shifted image filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge filtration is the image filtration $F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$. In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures. (ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees, i.e. cochain complexes $K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, and with $H^q(K^p)$ a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$ for all $p,q$. Form its simple complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration $L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of $H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.
items.strategy:
Route: Deligne III Scholie (8.1.9) and Theorem (8.1.15), transferred with the cohomological filtered-complex construction. Step 1 (weight spectral sequence). Apply the published cohomological filtered complex construction to $K$ with the decreasing filtration $F_{\mathrm{wt}}^p:=W_{-p}K$, which is degreewise finite by the definition. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$; the axiom of the mixed Hodge complex makes this a pure Hodge structure of weight $(p+q)+(-p)=q$ with its induced $F$, and its abutment is the image filtration $F^p_{\mathrm{wt}}H^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{-p}K))$, i.e. $W_mH^n$ under the shift $m=n-p$. Step 2 (degeneration at $E_2$). The differentials $d_r$ are induced by the differentials of the complex, so they preserve the rational structure and $F$; hence each $d_r$ is a morphism of the pure Hodge structures on the pages. By Step 1 and induction, $E_r^{p,q}$ is pure of weight $q$ for all $r\ge1$: $d_1$ is a morphism between pure structures of weight $q$ (in $E_1^{p,q}\to E_1^{p+1,q}$ both second indices are $q$), so its kernel and image are pure of weight $q$ by the strictness lemma, and $E_2^{p,q}=\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_1$ is pure of weight $q$. For $r\ge2$ the target $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ has weight $q-r+1<q$, and a morphism of mixed Hodge structures cannot map a pure weight-$q$ structure to a pure weight-$(q-r+1)$ structure (their weight filtrations force the image into $W_{q-r+1}$ of the target, which is zero); hence every $d_r$, $r\ge2$, vanishes and the sequence stabilizes at $E_2$. Step 3 (filtration identification). The abutment isomorphism $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n\cong E_\infty^{n-m,m}$ of Step 1 identifies complexes of vector spaces; the $F$-filtrations agree as well. For this, correct representatives: a class of $F^pH^n$ has a representative in $F^pK^n$; its image in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mK$ is a cycle in $F^p$, and the obstruction to lifting it to a cycle of $F^pK^n\cap W_mK^n$ is its differential, which lies in the image of $d$ and in $F^p$; strictness of the differential on the next lower weight-graded piece supplies a correction in $F^p$, and finiteness of $W$ terminates the descent. The construction is compatible with the page filtration because all $d_r$ are strict for $F$ on the relevant pages (they are morphisms of pure Hodge structures, using the strictness lemma), so the recursive filtration on the stable page is the one induced from the complex. Step 4 (functoriality). A morphism of mixed Hodge complexes preserves both filtrations and the comparison, so the induced map on $H^n$ preserves the image filtrations and is a mixed Hodge morphism by definition. Step 5 (cosimplicial case). The simple complex of the cosimplicial system is the total complex of the associated first-quadrant cochain bicomplex; the cosimplicial identities make the total differential square to zero and give $\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}(sK)\cong K^p[-p]$, and the filtration $L$ is finite in each degree because $p,q\ge0$ force $0\le p\le n$ in degree $n$. By hypothesis $H^q(K^p)$ is pure of weight $q$, so $H^n(\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}sK)=H^{n-p}(K^p)$ is pure of weight $n-p=n+(-p)$: the axiom of the mixed Hodge complex holds with filtration index $-p$, and Step 1 applies with $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)$. Setting $q:=m$ gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, and $q=n-p\le n$ because $p\ge0$. The construction of the simple complex is carried inside this proof; no separate cosimplicial totalization
supplier is assumed. The comparison map of sK is a filtered quasi-isomorphism because the filtration is
finite in each total degree and on each graded piece Gr^L_{-p}sK = K^p[-p] it is the given levelwise
filtered comparison, so the finite-filtration induction on the two-term filtrations applies; the internal
differential on each K^p is F-strict by the weight-zero Hodge complex hypothesis. Nothing in Steps 1-5
uses a choice principle or a splitting of the filtration.
items.axiom_use: None intended: the published filtered-complex spectral sequence construction is algebraic and choice-free, and Steps 1-5 use finite-dimensional linear algebra. The Step-3 author must re-verify the AC status of the spectral-sequence and double-complex suppliers, none of which states a choice principle.

title: Mixed Hodge Structures And Strictness Examples

items.title: A mixed Hodge extension without a rational splitting
items.statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure can be an extension of two pure structures and still admit no splitting over $\mathbb Q$. On $H=\mathbb Q e_0\oplus\mathbb Q e_1$ put $W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$, and $F^1=0$, $F^0=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, $F^{-1}=H_{\mathbb C}$. This is a mixed Hodge structure sitting in a short exact sequence $0\to\mathbb Q(1)\to H\to\mathbb Q(0)\to0$ which has no splitting in the category of rational mixed Hodge structures.
items.strategy: Verification in two steps, both finite computations in the displayed basis. Step 1: compute the graded pieces. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}=\mathbb Q e_1$ the filtration $F$ has $F^{-1}$ everything and $F^0=0$, so the Hodge type is $(-1,-1)$ and the piece is $\mathbb Q(1)$; on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0=\mathbb Q e_0$ the image of $F^0$ in the quotient is everything and $F^1=0$, so the type is $(0,0)$ and the piece is $\mathbb Q(0)$. Both are $n$-opposed for their weights, so the axioms hold, and the degree-one map $\mathbb Q(1)\to H$ and the quotient map $H\to\mathbb Q(0)$ are morphisms of mixed Hodge structures with kernel and cokernel as displayed. Step 2: rule out rational splittings. A $\mathbb Q$-linear section of the quotient sends the rational generator of $\mathbb Q(0)$ to $e_0+\lambda e_1$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb Q$. A morphism of mixed Hodge structures must map $F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ into $F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, so $e_0+\lambda e_1\in\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, forcing $\lambda=i$ by comparison of the $e_0$- and $e_1$-coefficients. No rational $\lambda$ does this, so no rational splitting exists. The verification uses only the definitions; it exhibits the non-split extension concretely and claims nothing about extensions of other weights or about integral structures.
items.axiom_use: None: the two computations use the rational basis and the displayed filtrations only.
